mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a short-term decline in S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
regime_hint: tightening cycle after a period of easing
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from a pre-tightening baseline (p > 0.05) during confirmed tightening phases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) followed by a subsequent decline in monthly pay growth (indicated by a steep drop in INDPRO) predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as investor sentiment deteriorates.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases then INDPRO falls in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive despite the labor signal pattern in 80% of similar episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in home sales (HOUST) above 2% of the prior month's level coincides with a positive S&P 20-day forward return as it signals resilient consumer demand.
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 20-day horizon during confirmed housing expansion periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive 2-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below trend is a leading indicator of supply-side constraints and predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negatively correlated with INDPRO declines in 5 out of 10 supply-shock episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4% for the first time in three months, a persistent rise in S&P 20-day forward returns is expected due to optimism about labor market strength.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4% after two consecutive months ≥ 4.0%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns fail to outperform a 4% UNRATE baseline (p > 0.05) in 60% of such regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 10,000 jobs followed by a sustained drop in inflation-adjusted wage growth (CPIAUCSL) predicts negative S&P 60-day forward returns due to wage-stagnation fears.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 10,000 and CPIAUCSL < previous month in the same quarter
regime_hint: wage growth cooling in labor market expansion
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically negative during 5 consecutive wage-cooling episodes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in retail sales (implied by a positive HOUST) combined with a decline in consumer confidence (not directly observable here, but proxy via a composite demand signal) predicts a positive 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are flat or negative during 3 consecutive positive HOUST months without external confirmation signals.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive declines in both industrial production (INDPRO) and raw material prices (not available in this catalog, so omitted) would indicate supply disruption, but here we use INDPRO decline alone as a proxy for risk. This predicts a negative S&P 60-day forward return when INDPRO falls by >5% in a month.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns do not show significant negative relationship with INDPRO declines in 4 out of 7 contraction episodes (p > 0.10).
